title: Closed subschemes of a geometric fibre over a finite field are defined over a finite extension
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], so $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, with subfields $\mathbf F_{q^m}\subset k$. Let $X_0$ be a scheme of finite type over $k_0$, $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and $g_X=\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma):X\to X$ the geometric Frobenius automorphism of [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Let $i:C\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion. Then there are an integer $m\ge1$ and a closed subscheme $C_m\subseteq X_0\times_{k_0}\mathbf F_{q^m}$ whose base change along $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_{q^m}$ is $i(C)$ as a closed subscheme of $X=(X_0\times_{k_0}\mathbf F_{q^m})\times_{\mathbf F_{q^m}}k$. Consequently there is an automorphism of schemes $\varphi:C\to C$ with $i\circ\varphi=g_X^m\circ i$.
The finite-type, closed-immersion and base-change notions are those of [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] and [def-pc-base-change].

source.place: Final paragraph: finite coefficients and descent to one finite constant-field extension

proof.text: Index by the finitely generated k₀-subalgebras A of k, ordered by inclusion. Bottom gives an index and the join of two finitely generated subalgebras is finitely generated, so this is directed. The explicit filtered-colimit theorem CommRingCat.isColimitFGSubalgebraCocone identifies its colimit with k. Spec preserves the opposite limit. Pullbacks commute with connected limits (isLimitOfIsPullbackOfIsConnected), giving a limiting cone of X_A = X₀ × Spec A with vertex X₀ × Spec k. The transition maps are base changes of maps between affine schemes, hence affine.

source.place: Final paragraph: finite coefficients and descent to one finite constant-field extension

proof.text: Each A is a finitely generated algebra over the field k₀ and hence Noetherian. Each X_A is locally Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] and finite-type base change [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Its quasi-compact structure map to affine Spec A makes it quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. The same argument makes X locally Noetherian.

source.place: Final paragraph: finite coefficients and descent to one finite constant-field extension

proof.text: The closed immersion i is locally of finite type and quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Its locally Noetherian target makes it locally of finite presentation by [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth], giving finite presentation as in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Apply clause (1) of [thm-pd-spreading-out] directly to i over the ambient system X_A: Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation supplies Y → X_A and a cartesian square recovering i. The eventual closed-immersion theorem [lemma-nagata-closed-immersion-stage-exists], in its pullback-square form Scheme.exists_isClosedImmersion_pullback_snd, supplies a later stage where the descended map is closed. isPullback_isPullbackLift preserves the square. This descends the source and embedding together; the separate morphism clause of spreading out is unnecessary.

source.place: Final paragraph: finite coefficients and descent to one finite constant-field extension

proof.text: Since k/k₀ is algebraic, each A is integral over k₀ (isIntegral_algHom_iff). A finitely generated integral algebra is finite-dimensional (Algebra.IsIntegral.finite), and an algebraic subalgebra of a field is a field (Algebra.IsAlgebraic.toIntermediateField). Its cardinality is q^m for m = finrank k₀ A ≥ 1, by Module.natCard_eq_pow_finrank. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-unique-subfield-of-closure] identifies this subfield with extensionSubfield m hm. The resulting ring equivalence commutes with inclusions into k; injectivity of the subfield inclusion makes it commute with the base embedding as well.

source.place: Final paragraph: finite coefficients and descent to one finite constant-field extension

proof.text: Base change by the spectrum of this field equivalence identifies X_A with X₀ × Spec(extensionSubfield m hm). Compose the descended closed embedding with the inverse of that isomorphism. Transport the cartesian square, then paste it with the ambient base-change square. Its canonical isoPullback, bundled by Over.isoMk, is the required isomorphism over Spec k. The first-projection equations give exactly the required equation with the embedding into X₀; no underlying reduced subscheme is taken.

source.place: Final paragraph: finite coefficients and descent to one finite constant-field extension

proof.text: Let σ be geometric field Frobenius and E = extensionSubfield m hm. Its cardinality q^m from [lem-weil-unique-subfield-of-closure] implies σ^m fixes E pointwise, by FiniteField.geometricFrobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic_pow_apply_of_card_eq. Thus Spec(σ^m) and its inverse are over Spec E. The cartesian square lifts the identity on Y and the coefficient automorphism to an endomorphism of C, and similarly lifts the inverse. Pullback uniqueness proves the two composites are identities. Induction using galoisMap_projections from [def-weil-frobenius-detailed] gives the projections of the mth power of ambient geometric Frobenius. Comparing both ambient projections proves φ.hom ≫ i = i ≫ (D.geometricFrobenius X₀ ^ m).hom.
